title: Most People Miss This Detail in The Empty Pit
paragraphs: Most People Miss This Detail in The Empty Pit
Most people read the story and remember the betrayal.

The coat.
The brothers.
The pit.
But they miss the detail that should shake your soul:
“The pit was empty; there was no water in it.” (Genesis 37:24)
Empty.

No water.
No comfort.
No way to survive long.
No echo of mercy from the people above him.

Joseph was not dropped into inconvenience.
He was dropped into a place that looked like the end.
And that is exactly where many of us meet God.

Not in the palace.
Not in the promotion.
Not in the applause.
In the empty pit.

The place where what used to sustain you is gone.
The place where nobody explains why.
The place where heaven feels silent and the faces you trusted are the ones who pushed you in.
But here’s what most people miss:
The pit was empty, but God was not absent.

What looked like abandonment was not the end of Joseph’s story.
It was the dark hallway to purpose.
The pit did not cancel the promise.
It only stripped Joseph of every illusion that he could save himself.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because the Gospel works the same way.
Jesus entered the deepest pit of human sin, shame, rejection, and death itself.
He took the emptiness we deserved.
He carried our judgment on the cross.
And when the tomb was found empty, it declared that the pit does not get the final word.

Not for Joseph.
Not for Jesus.
Not for you.
So if your life feels like an empty pit right now, hear me clearly:
What feels empty may be the very place where God is breaking pride, exposing false saviors, and preparing resurrection-shaped faith in you.

Repent of trusting comfort more than Christ.
Repent of thinking the pit means God has left.
Look to Jesus.

Because in Christ, your lowest place can become holy ground.
From betrayal to calling.
From the pit to the presence of God.

The pit may be empty.
But if Christ is with you, you are not.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
